transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this design review started. We've got the async report-generation service going to production next Wednesday, so we need to get sign-off sorted today. I can see the current draft uses standard queue mode, max batch size of 200, 90-day retention, and ordinary application logging. Before I can approve the production architecture, I need platform engineering and compliance to weigh in. Let's go through the checklist — does anyone have blocking requirements to raise?

transcript.text: I have a blocking requirement. This morning while load-testing an unrelated ingestion worker, I confirmed that the queue service's standard mode can reorder report jobs during a broker failover. The provider's documented configuration requires FIFO mode and a maximum batch size of exactly 50 for ordered report delivery. I haven't updated the architecture draft yet, but the current standard queue mode and batch size of 200 won't work — we need FIFO mode and a max batch size of 50.

transcript.text: I have blocking compliance requirements. During a compliance consultation yesterday, I confirmed that these billing and usage reports must be automatically purged after exactly 30 days — not the 90-day retention in the current draft. Additionally, every report download requires an immutable audit record containing the account and requesting user. Ordinary application logging won't satisfy that. I haven't filed the compliance note against this service yet, but these are both blockers for production sign-off.

Update the architecture draft to reflect 30-day automatic report retention (down from 90 days) and immutable audit records for every report download capturing account and requesting user, replacing ordinary application logging.
